propositions: The completion close workflow reads git HEAD independently during verify and sign phases, allowing a concurrent commit to land between them and cause verify to check one tree state while sign refuses to attest a different tree state

When HEAD drift occurs between verify and sign, the ticket is closed without a completion attestation despite the verification phase succeeding, leaving it in an unrecoverable state (re-close is a no-op, only --force-close or manual manifest fabrication available)

The default (no --ref) path in completion close is vulnerable to TOCTOU splits even after the 80af --ref fix, because HEAD is resolved twice independently rather than pinned once for the verify+sign+close unit
A benign unrelated commit landing between verify and sign should not invalidate a completion attestation that was successfully verified against a stable, immutable revision
